title: Tenant capacity fallback scenarios — regional mix (May 2027)
summary: Working sheet to model per-contract Dedicated reservations with regional redistribution and fallback policies. Goal: validate that contracted reserved GPUs + buffer + burst pool keep latency SLOs across NA/EU/APAC under 3 demand scenarios (baseline, seasonal peak, and cluster outage). This is an operational input for the Q3-2027 capacity runbook and will feed into the reservation rebalancing proposal.

notes:
Assumptions and modelling details:
- Baseline utilization uses trailing 90d p50 token throughput per tenant scaled to reserved GPUs. Peak factor is multiplicative demand during 95th percentile windows (daily/seasonal).
- Buffer_pct is applied on top of reserved_gpus to size soft-safety margins before invoking fallback. Allocated_burst is explicit GPUs we plan to borrow from the global burst pool under the SLA.
- Fallback_policy hierarchy (ordered): 1) allocate burst-pool; 2) region shift to compatible variant (same model family) in prespecified partner region; 3) degrade to quantized/cheaper model variant with lower token cost; 4) apply tenant-specific rate-limits or queueing.
- Regional routing constraints: data residency tenants (e.g., MedPrompt) cannot cross region; fallback limited to on-prem or edge.
- Outage scenario (modeled separately): simulate 20% of regional capacity unavailable for 3h; check which contracts exceed buffer and require forced degrading.
- Cost impact: quantify delta in GPU-hours and incremental cloud egress per re-route. Early estimate: shifting 10% of reserved hours to cross-region adds ~0.6% egress cost for average tenant.

Model outputs and quick interpretations:
- Under baseline scenario, all tenants fit reserved + buffer except Queryium and StudioForge which rely on burst-pool for nightly peaks.
- Under seasonal peak (peak_factor applied) three tenants (AtlasRetail, HyperNarrative, FinSight) would exhaust buffer and need cross-region burst followed by degradation if burst exhausted.
- Under regional outage test (us-west-2 20% down), Vectorita Labs would need both cross-region shift and 50% of its peak served by degraded variant to keep latency SLOs.
Notes on conservative sizing: increase buffer_pct by +5 for tenants with >1.4 peak_factor and baseline_util_pct >60 to reduce automated fallbacks.
